name: Xiao Jian
current_role: Chairman and CEO, CMGE Technology Group (HKEX: 0302)
profile: Xiao Jian (b. ~1980) is co-founder, chairman and CEO of CMGE Technology Group, a Hong Kong-listed Chinese mobile game publisher and IP game operator. Joined CMGE Group as COO in 2011 and became CEO in 2012; CMGE has built its strategy around licensed IP such as Chinese Paladin (Xianjian), Xuanyuan Sword and Monopoly (Da Fu Weng).
interesting_fact: In 2018 CMGE paid RMB213m for 51% of Beijing Softstar (later 100%), securing development rights around classic Taiwanese IPs like Chinese Paladin/Sword and Fairy; Xiao has framed CMGE as an 'IP game operator' spreading Chinese culture via games.
deep_cut_fact: Before CMGE, Xiao founded mobile game developer Huiyou Digital (Shenzhen) in July 2007, sold to HK-listed V1 Group (Crazy Sports) in Oct 2009. He earned a law degree via online education (South China Normal Univ., 2009) and a master's in software engineering from Beihang University (2014).
notes: IR email is the shareholder-enquiry contact named in the 2021 annual report (named IR staffer); may be outdated, check latest annual report. Gaming, not energy; angle could be AI in game dev (he has discussed AI in interviews).

name: Vasyl Khmelnytsky
current_role: Founder, UFuture investment holding (Kyiv/Brussels) and K.FUND foundation
profile: Ukrainian entrepreneur and former MP (1998-2002, 2006-2014). Built wealth in real estate, infrastructure and steel (sold a Zaporizhstal stake in 2006 for ~$400m), then founded UFuture (2017), which holds UDP, Kyiv's Sikorsky (Zhuliany) airport, IT firms and stakes in Biopharma and UDP Renewables, plus the UNIT.City innovation park.
interesting_fact: He set out to build a 'Silicon Valley match' in Ukraine via UNIT.City in Kyiv; UFuture also backs UDP Renewables (wind/solar) and his K.FUND has run humanitarian aid since the 2022 invasion.
deep_cut_fact: Born 1966 in Bayanaul, Kazakhstan, to a tractor driver and a house-painter, he trained as a fitter-welder (vocational school in Vatutine, 1984) and worked as a gas-electric welder and foreman in Leningrad before business; he earned a law degree from Kyiv's Shevchenko University in 2002.
notes: Energy angle: UDP Renewables (wind/solar) and industrial parks. UN Global Compact ambassador (2021). Speaks at Kyiv International Economic Forum; best route is via UFuture/K.FUND press office.

name: Duan Peizhang
current_role: Controlling shareholder and director, Shanghai Longyun Cultural Creation & Technology Group (ST Longyun, 603729.SH)
profile: Duan Peizhang co-founded Longyun, a Shanghai advertising/media-buying company, with Fang Xiaoqin in 2003 and took it public on the Shanghai exchange in 2015. He was chairman and GM 2008-2015 and has sat on the board since 2008; after a June 2026 internal transfer he holds ~30% and is sole actual controller.
interesting_fact: Longyun's business spans TV/media advertising agency, digital marketing and (more recently) liquor sales, and it has tried to expand into film/TV content via Yuheng Pictures.
notes: Low public profile; little biography published. Company is under ST (risk-warning) status since April 2026 and loss-making - avoid as an outreach hook. Reach via company board secretary office (see SSE filings).

name: Kenneth T. Sim
current_role: Co-Founder and Executive Chairman, Astrana Health (NASDAQ: ASTH)
profile: Dr. Kenneth Sim is a general surgeon who co-founded Network Medical Management and built it, via a 2017 merger with Apollo Medical, into Astrana Health (formerly ApolloMed), a physician-centric, value-based care platform in Southern California and beyond. He is Executive Chairman; his son Brandon Sim is CEO. He also chairs Allied Pacific IPA (APC).
interesting_fact: He led development of 'Super Medical Centers' across Southern California, integrated sites combining surgery, lab, radiology and urgent care under one roof.
deep_cut_fact: He trained at Loma Linda and the Autonomous University of Guadalajara in Mexico, did his general surgery residency at LA County King/Drew Medical Center, and won the LA County Medical Association's Independent Physician Leadership Award in 2014.
notes: Healthcare, not energy. Also on governing boards of Alhambra Hospital Medical Center, Garfield Medical Center and AHMC Seton. Son Brandon Sim (CEO) is the more public-facing figure.

name: Padmasingh Isaac
current_role: Founder and Chairman/Managing Director, Aachi Group (Aachi Masala Foods), Chennai
profile: A.D. Padmasingh Isaac, a first-generation entrepreneur from Nazareth in Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu, spent about a decade in sales at Godrej before founding Aachi Masala in Chennai in the mid-1990s. Aachi grew from cheap curry-masala sachets aimed at rural buyers into a 1,000-crore-plus spice and packaged-food group selling in dozens of countries.
interesting_fact: Aachi's first products were curry masala powders in low-priced sachets; when shopkeepers were reluctant to stock them, he personally promoted the brand outside shops. Aachi was named 'India's No. 1 Most Trusted Brand 2015' (Trust Research Advisory).
deep_cut_fact: He is the author of a business book, 'Enjoy Success, Relish Failures' (Rupa Publications), and has held advisory roles at the Indian Institute of Crop Processing Technology, Thanjavur, and NIFTEM, Haryana.
notes: care@ is the company's general customer-care address, not a personal or press office. Aachi was reported in 2024 to be in acquisition talks with large FMCG groups (unconfirmed). Speaks often at youth/entrepreneurship events in Tamil Nadu - a Tamil-language podcast angle may land well.

name: Yan Dapeng
current_role: Vice Chairman and Chief Engineer, Wuhan Raycus Fiber Laser Technologies (300747.SZ)
profile: Dr. Yan Dapeng is a laser physicist who returned from the US in 2007 to co-found Wuhan Raycus with Huagong Laser, building China's leading domestic fiber-laser maker and challenging IPG Photonics' dominance. Raycus listed in Shenzhen in 2018; Yan remains vice chairman and chief engineer, recognised as a 'national outstanding engineer'.
interesting_fact: In 2026 Raycus unveiled a single-mode 10,000-watt fiber laser (10.1 kW, beam quality M2 as low as 1.13); Yan described the Raman effect as a 'traffic jam' of light energy in the fiber that limits power scaling.
deep_cut_fact: From 1996 to 2007 he worked in the US at the University of Illinois at Chicago, Wright State University and fiber-laser firms including Nufern, earning three US patents, after earlier working at Nanjing Polytechnic; he and Huagong Laser each put RMB30m into Raycus in 2007.
notes: Raycus is now majority-owned by state-backed China Aerospace Science & Industry (via Huagong lineage). Deep-cut source is a 2010 industry blog citing Raycus' website - verify before use. Technical person; lasers for battery/EV manufacturing link to energy theme.

name: Anwar Patel
profile: Anwer (Anwar) Patel, a Bolton pharmacist, co-founded the Cohens Chemist group with his elder brother Yakub in 1979 (first pharmacy in Rochdale). He died on 28 April 2021, aged 66.
notes: Deceased 28 April 2021 per Pharmacy Business (https://www.pharmacy.biz/news/cohens-chemist-co-founder-anwer-patel-dies-aged-66). Rich-list name is spelled 'Anwer' in trade press. Brother/co-founder Yakub Patel may be a living alternative.

name: Julian Dunkerton
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Superdry (taken private 2024); owner of Dunkertons Cider and The Lucky Onion hospitality group
profile: Julian Dunkerton (b. 1965) started the Cult Clothing chain at 19 and co-founded Superdry in 2003, building it into a global Japanese-inspired fashion brand listed in London. He left in 2018, won a 2019 shareholder vote to return as CEO, and took the company private in 2024 after a restructuring. He also runs Dunkertons Organic Cider and Cotswolds hotels/pubs.
interesting_fact: He co-founded his first fashion business, Cult Clothing Co, at age 19 with partner Ian Hibbs and a £2,000 loan - the retail chain that later spawned Superdry.
deep_cut_fact: His father Ivor and stepmother Susie founded Dunkertons Organic Cider in Herefordshire; Julian took control in 2014 and in 2016 moved it to a new cidery at Dowdeswell Park near Cheltenham.
notes: Outspoken, media-friendly; known for a £1m donation to the People's Vote campaign (2018). Avoid Superdry's 2023-24 losses/restructuring as a hook. Cotswolds hospitality and cider are good conversational angles.

name: Charlie Watts
profile: Charlie Watts, drummer of the Rolling Stones from 1963, died on 24 August 2021 in London, aged 80.

name: Robin Raina
current_role: Former Chairman, President & CEO of Ebix Inc. (suspended; Ebix assets sold in Chapter 11)
profile: Kashmir-born, Patiala-raised industrial engineer who joined Delphi Information Systems in 1997 and, as CEO from 1999, built it into Ebix, an Atlanta-based insurance-software and fintech roll-up with large Indian operations (EbixCash). Ebix filed for Chapter 11 in December 2023 after a loan default and its businesses were sold.
interesting_fact: Under Raina, Ebix was ranked No. 4 on Fortune's list of the 100 fastest-growing companies, and he was named the top-performing CEO in Georgia by the Atlanta Business Chronicle.
deep_cut_fact: He studied at Our Lady of Fatima Convent High School in Patiala, graduated in industrial engineering from Thapar Institute in 1989, and began his career at Pertech Computers (promoted to area manager in 1990) before moving to Singapore with Mindware in 1993.
notes: Sensitive: Ebix bankruptcy (2023) and suspension as CEO; Hurun 2019 wealth figure is likely much reduced. Robin Raina Foundation site (robinrainafoundation.org) currently 'coming soon'. No current published contact found. Low priority for outreach.

name: Randolph L Marten
current_role: Chairman of the Board and CEO, Marten Transport Ltd. (NASDAQ: MRTN), Mondovi, Wisconsin
profile: Randy Marten joined the family trucking firm founded by his father Roger in 1946, became president at its 1986 Nasdaq IPO and CEO in 1993, turning a Wisconsin milk-route business into a ~3,500-truck temperature-controlled carrier operating from Mexico to Canada. He moved to executive chairman, then resumed the CEO role after Timothy Kohl retired in September 2025.
interesting_fact: Marten Transport began in 1946 when Roger Marten, aged 17, bought a milk-delivery route from the Modena Co-op Creamery with a $400 loan from his mother.
deep_cut_fact: Randy won Ernst & Young's Entrepreneur of the Year award for transportation in the Wisconsin region in 2005; for the company's 50th anniversary in 1996 Marten opened the Roger Marten Community Center in Mondovi.
notes: Low media profile; best route is corporate office in Mondovi, WI via contact page or IR. Energy angle: fleet fuel efficiency (APUs, $16m commitment in 2007), refrigerated/intermodal logistics.

name: Luis A Muller
current_role: President and CEO, Cohu, Inc. (NASDAQ: COHU); Director, Ralliant Corp.
profile: Dr. Luis Müller is a Brazilian-born mechanical engineer who has led Cohu, a San Diego-based semiconductor test and inspection equipment maker, as CEO since December 2014. He joined Cohu's Delta Design unit in 2005 after nine years at Teradyne, ran its Rasco GmbH unit in Germany and the Semiconductor Equipment Group, and expanded Cohu via the 2018 Xcerra acquisition.
interesting_fact: He also sits on the board of Ralliant Corporation, the precision-test and sensor company spun out of Fortive in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his B.S. and M.S. in mechanical engineering at Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina in Brazil and a PhD in mechanical engineering from MIT; earlier at Cohu he ran high-speed pick-and-place handler products and managed Rasco GmbH in Germany (2009-2010).
notes: Semiconductor test equipment - relevant to AI/data-center chip supply chain (HBM, compute test). Route via Cohu investor relations; Ralliant directorship per Cohu bio.

name: Guy Harwood
current_role: Retired racehorse trainer (Coombelands, Pulborough); family behind the Harwoods motor dealership group
profile: Guy Harwood (b. 1939, Pulborough, West Sussex) comes from the Harwoods car-dealership family business founded by his father Wally in 1931. He became one of Britain's leading Flat trainers from Coombelands stables, training Dancing Brave to win the 1986 Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe; his daughter Amanda Perrett took over the yard in 1996.
interesting_fact: He trained Dancing Brave, winner of the 2,000 Guineas, Eclipse, King George and the 1986 Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, and European Horse of the Year 1986.
deep_cut_fact: In the 1970s he made Coombelands one of Britain's most modern yards, introducing artificial gallops, American-style barns and a computerised office system; before training he rode 40 point-to-point and 14 National Hunt winners.
notes: Aged 87 and retired; very low public profile, no published personal contact. Alive status based on Wikipedia 'Living people' category, not independently re-verified. Not a natural fit for an energy/data-centre podcast.

name: Suresh Tyagi
current_role: Vice Chairman & Whole-Time Director, Gold Plus Glass Industry Ltd (New Delhi)
profile: Suresh Tyagi is vice chairman of Gold Plus Glass, the family glass group led by his brother, chairman Subhash Tyagi. It grew from a 1985 glass-trading business into architectural glass processing (Sonepat, Kala Amb) and, from 2009, float glass manufacturing in Roorkee; Gold Plus now claims about 26% of India's float-glass capacity and is the country's second-largest maker.
interesting_fact: In 2009 Gold Plus began float-glass production at Roorkee, describing itself as the first fully Indian-owned company to do so, and added a 700 TPD second float line in 2018. Its tagline is 'Apna Desh, Apna Glass'.
deep_cut_fact: The group's origin story: Subhash Tyagi started in 1985 as a glass trader with Rs 5,000 of capital and became India's largest glass trader by the early 1990s before moving into processing in 1996.
notes: Few personal details published about Suresh himself; deep-cut fact is about the family business (his brother's founding story). info@ is the general corporate inbox. Energy angle: float glass is an input for solar panels and energy-efficient buildings.

name: Nikolai Mykola Udianskyi
current_role: Co-owner, Parlament Media Group; Honorary Consul of Romania in Kharkiv
profile: Mykola Udianskyi (b. 1983, Kharkiv) is a Ukrainian IT/crypto entrepreneur who co-founded Prof-IT (2013, with Bohdan Prylepa), a developer of crypto-exchange and blockchain software, and co-founded the Coinsbit exchange; he formerly owned LocalTrade. Forbes Ukraine ranked him No. 59 among the richest Ukrainians in 2021 (~$180m).
interesting_fact: Before crypto he spent 2006-2014 manufacturing and distributing payment/trade terminals, and he holds a PhD in law.
deep_cut_fact: He served in Ukraine's armed forces in 2001-2003 in the radiation, chemical and biological reconnaissance troops, and graduated from Kharkiv Automobile and Highway University in 2009 in 'roads and airfields' engineering.
notes: Caution: Ukrainian Wikipedia records fraud allegations against his crypto projects and criticism over alleged Russia/criminal links - reputational due diligence advised before featuring. No published personal contact found.
